chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from al-Hasan ibn Ali, from Dawud ibn Kathir al-Raqqi, who said:

I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): 'May I be your ransom, indeed a man from the companions of Abu al-Khattab forbade me from eating the bukhth (a type of turtle/tortoise) and from eating the musarral pigeon.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'There is no harm in riding the bukhth, drinking its milk, eating its meat, and eating the musarral pigeon.'

key_terms.أَصْحَابِ أَبِي الْخَطَّابِ: The companions/followers of Abu al-Khattab (a known jurist)
key_terms.الْبُخْت: A type of turtle or tortoise, often marine
key_terms.الْمُسَرَّوَل: A specific type or variety of pigeon

ai.seo_question: What is the Shia ruling on eating turtles and specific types of pigeons?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Istibsar*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) validates the permissibility of consuming the *bukhth* (often identified as the sea turtle or tortoise) and *musarral* pigeon, directly countering the restrictive view of a companion of Abu al-Khattab. The ruling is comprehensive, extending not only to eating the meat but also to riding the animal and consuming its milk, highlighting the flexibility in Shia jurisprudence regarding specific marine and avian species.
